title: Characterization of the predicate bit
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over Boolean symbols, let $d,c,A,a$ be natural numbers, let $x$ be a finite Boolean string, and let $\tau:\mathbb{N}\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$. Suppose the configuration-code length $vlen(N,d,c,|x|)$ is at most the block width $vwid(A,a,|x|)$. Form the finite string whose entries are $\tau(0),\ldots,\tau(3w^2+3w-1)$, where $w=vwid(A,a,|x|)$, and pair-encode it with $x$. The predicate bit on this encoded input is true if and only if both the initial-configuration check on the length-$vlen(N,d,c,|x|)$ prefix of the block of width $w$ starting at offset $w$, and the accepting-configuration check on the corresponding prefix of the block starting at offset $2w$, hold, and at least one of the following holds: for some $i<w$, the adjacent triples of width-$w$ blocks at levels $i$ and $i+1$ fail the selector relation; or the final two blocks at level $w$ satisfy the block-step relation.
hypotheses_covered: A finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ over Boolean symbols
caveat: The initial, accepting, block-step, and selector relations are named in the payload but their underlying coding definitions are not informally specified; the statement describes their roles and offsets rather than expanding their full definitions.
